facts.text: East Vandergrift sits in the Kiskiminetas Valley, once home to Delaware and Shawnee Indians before European settlers arrived.
In 1895 Apollo Iron and Steel built a steelworks and hired Olmsted, Olmsted and Eliot to design a model industrial town that became Vandergrift.
The borough’s compact boundaries are defined by its adjacency to Vandergrift borough to the west and the Kiskiminetas River to the south, shaping its southeastern edge.
East Vandergrift’s history museum chronicles the town’s evolution from indigenous occupation to a thriving steel community.
The Victorian Vandergrift Museum & Historical Society, located in the borough, preserves artifacts from the town’s industrial heyday.
In recent decades, East Vandergrift has revitalized historic buildings through adaptive reuse and community projects that boost resident engagement.
